referencePolicy: Original game interpretation. Primary NECA pages returned403; approved fallback to original Moto antigrav de chasse. No1:1 or film-canon claim.

prompts.identity:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original bitmap game vehicle identity sheet for a 2D side-scrolling Yautja fan game, NOT an official prop replica.
Create ONE original Yautja hunting hover bike, an explicitly original interpretation called internally 'Moto antigrav de chasse'. Do not claim or reproduce an exact Predator Badlands or Kenner vehicle. This sheet must show exactly TWO large isolated orthographic side elevations of the SAME EMPTY vehicle: top row facing right, bottom row facing left. Full silhouette entirely inside canvas, same scale, generous empty padding and equal alignment. 1536x1024 landscape if possible. True transparent background with no checkerboard, no backdrop, no cast shadow, no ground, no labels, no text, no watermark.
Design a practical alien anti-gravity hunting motorcycle: low predatory wedge-like gunmetal chassis, weathered dark bronze ribbed plates, narrow pointed prow, low rear propulsion housing, one open saddle, anatomically credible thigh/knee clearance for a tall Yautja rider, a reachable handlebar and two visible footrests. No wheels. Subtle red inactive sensor glass, carved geometric alien engraving with no readable alphabet. Distinctive angular yet organic Yautja hunting aesthetics, not a generic human motorcycle or Star Wars speeder. Make the machine unoccupied: no creature, pilot, hands, skull cargo or trophies baked into it.
Two small clearly articulated parking stabilizers under the center/rear chassis are fully deployed, meeting one common imaginary ground line; their pivot sockets and hinge count are unambiguous. They are mechanical support feet, not weapons. Keep the two mirrored-side views logically consistent including handlebar, saddle, footrests, engine and stabilizer attachment points; draw each side as a plausible independent view.
Rendering: high-detail hand-painted bitmap game asset, sharply readable silhouette and layered metal construction, cinematic restrained highlights, no black comic outlines, no pixel grid. No muzzle flash, flame, smoke, exhaust glow, speed trail, lighting aura, floating UI or embedded VFX. Every form must remain readable against light or dark gameplay backgrounds. This is a reviewable vehicle model sheet, not an animation claim.
prompts.stabilizersInitial:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: real drawn 2D game animation sprite sheet for this original Yautja hover bike.
Input image is a VEHICLE IDENTITY REFERENCE, not a background or layout reference. Use the TOP, RIGHT-FACING vehicle design from the reference exactly: same bronze/gunmetal wedge chassis, long pointed prow, rear engine, saddle, handlebar, footrests, hinged parking struts, engraved plates and red inactive sensor glass. There must be NO rider and NO weapon firing.
Create EXACTLY EIGHT separate full right-facing orthographic side-view drawings arranged in a strict 2-COLUMN by 4-ROW sheet, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Landscape 1536x1024. Each frame fits safely inside its own 768x256 cell, with at least 36 pixels clear margin between subjects and 20 pixels outer page margin. Keep all eight fuselages at identical size, orientation and relative cell coordinates, approximately 620 pixels wide. The entire vehicle including nose, rear fin, grips and every support foot must be visible. Do not rotate the camera or change the bike's perspective or design between frames.
Action is a NONCOMBAT PARKING-STABILIZER DEPLOY/RETRACT cycle. Animate ONLY the two articulated underside support struts and their pads through real distinct drawings, keeping their two root pivot sockets immobile on the fuselage and retaining the same hinge count. The chassis itself stays motionless at one hover height.
Frame 1: both struts tucked nearly horizontal under the chassis.
Frame 2: both struts pivot down roughly 30 degrees, knees folding naturally.
Frame 3: extend to roughly 60 degrees.
Frame 4: fully deployed approximately 90 degrees, both support pads flat at their common low line.
Frame 5: start retracting, roughly 75 degrees, pads lift.
Frame 6: retract through roughly 50 degrees.
Frame 7: retract through roughly 25 degrees.
Frame 8: return fully tucked as a seamless return to frame 1.
The first and last pose may close the cycle but the middle poses MUST visibly show actual joint motion, not eight copies or a moved whole image. Stowed legs must not intersect the engine, footrest or saddle.
True transparent RGBA background, preserve actual alpha. No opaque checkerboard, colored backdrop, shadows, floor, labels, frame numbers, guide grid, text, watermark, muzzle flash, flame, glow, exhaust or smoke. Fuselage and VFX must remain independent; this sheet contains the bike and its support mechanics only.
Maintain the hand-painted high-detail bitmap style and crisp metal silhouette of the reference. This is an original game interpretation, not a claim of an official movie prop or canonical technology.
prompts.stabilizersBackgroundAndMechanicsCorrect:
Edit the displayed 8-frame hover-bike sprite sheet. Keep the exact original bike identity, bronze/gunmetal plates, saddle, handlebars, engine and all eight right-facing body silhouettes. Fix only these production defects:
1. Replace the entire opaque checkerboard and all background/shadow/haze between and inside the motorcycles with a SINGLE perfectly flat uniform saturated magenta #FF00FF (RGB255,0,255). This is an explicit color-key source, not pretend transparency. Absolutely no checkerboard, gray patches, gradients, ground or glow. No magenta paint on the vehicles.
2. Make BOTH parking support legs move progressively through the entire cycle. Two fixed circular root hinge sockets are attached to the UNDERBODY at about 32% and 50% of body length from the rear. These roots stay at exactly the same positions relative to the fuselage in every frame. Do not attach a leg to a handlebar, riding footrest, nose, exhaust or moving part. Both roots remain visible, even when legs are tucked. Each leg has exactly two linked rigid segments, one knee hinge and one flat pad. The foreground front leg must not pop into existence only in frame4; draw its gradual extension in frames2/3 and retraction in frames5/6/7.
Eight poses in reading order, 2 columns and 4 rows: tucked; 30-degree deployment; 60-degree deployment; fully deployed; 75-degree retract; 50-degree retract; 25-degree retract; tucked. Both legs follow the pose together, with both pads at the same low level when fully deployed. The fully deployed support legs are NOT riding footrests. No vehicle movement or squash.
3. Respect safe cell boundaries: same body size in all eight cells, maximum vehicle width 660 pixels for each 768px-wide cell, approximately 45 pixels margin on each side. No nose or rear fin touches a page or cell edge. Canvas1536x1024, each cell768x256. Entire vehicle silhouette including feet inside each cell.
No new vehicle, rider, VFX, fire, smoke, labels, frame numbers, guide borders or text. Red sensor glass is unchanged and inactive. Preserve all actual drawings as clean high-detail painted 2D game assets.
